why_use_this: Reach for this package when you have a polynomial equation or a small system of nonlinear equations and need the actual root(s), not a symbolic simplification -- vani-algebra finds numeric real roots, it doesn't do algebra on the equations themselves (that's [vani-symbolic](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-symbolic)'s job). Quadratics are already covered by the compiler's own `f64_quadratic_root` builtin; this package's real value starts at cubic (a genuine closed-form solution via Cardano's method) and continues through arbitrary degree (via a companion-matrix eigenvalue approach) and small nonlinear systems (via Newton's method, with both an analytic-Jacobian and a finite-difference-Jacobian entry point for when you can't or don't want to hand-derive the Jacobian). If your system is *linear*, skip this package entirely and call [vani-matrix](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-matrix)'s `mat_solve` directly -- there's nothing here for that case. And if you need complex roots (not just real ones), this package's power-iteration eigenvalue solver won't find them -- see the README's "Scope" section for why that's a deliberate, documented limitation rather than a bug.

math_notes.algebra_poly_from_roots: Builds the monic polynomial \( p(x) = \prod_{i} (x - r_i) \) whose roots are exactly the given \( r_i \), by repeated synthetic multiplication -- the exact inverse operation of root-finding, useful for constructing test cases with known-exact roots.
math_notes.algebra_cubic_roots_real: Solves \( a x^3 + b x^2 + c x + d = 0 \) via Cardano's method: substitute \( x = t - b/(3a) \) to eliminate the quadratic term, giving the depressed cubic \( t^3 + pt + q = 0 \), then branch on the discriminant \( \Delta = -4p^3 - 27q^2 \) -- the trigonometric formula \( t_k = 2\sqrt{-p/3} \, \cos\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\arccos\!\left(\tfrac{3q}{2p}\sqrt{-3/p}\right) - \tfrac{2\pi k}{3}\right) \) when \( \Delta \ge 0 \) (3 real roots), the two-cube-root (Cardano) formula when \( \Delta < 0 \) (1 real root).
math_notes.algebra_poly_companion: Builds the companion matrix \( C \) of a monic polynomial \( x^n + c_{n-1}x^{n-1} + \cdots + c_0 \) -- an \( n \times n \) matrix whose eigenvalues are exactly the polynomial's roots. This implementation uses the "bottom companion" convention: 1s on the subdiagonal (\( C_{i+1,i} = 1 \)) and the negated, monic-normalized coefficients \( -c_{n-1}, \ldots, -c_0 \) down the last column. This is what turns "find polynomial roots" into "find matrix eigenvalues", the whole reason `mat_eig_power` is usable here at all.
math_notes.algebra_newton_system: Newton's method for a system of \( n \) nonlinear equations \( F(x) = 0 \): iterate \( x_{k+1} = x_k - J(x_k)^{-1} F(x_k) \), where \( J \) is the (caller-supplied, analytic) Jacobian \( J_{ij} = \partial F_i / \partial x_j \). Each step solves the linear system \( J(x_k) \, \delta = -F(x_k) \) via `mat_solve` rather than explicitly inverting \( J \).
math_notes.algebra_newton_system_damped: Same Newton step as `algebra_newton_system`, \( x_{k+1} = x_k + \alpha \, \delta_k \) with \( \delta_k = -J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k) \), but with a backtracking line search choosing \( \alpha \in (0, 1] \) (halving until \( \lVert F(x_k+\alpha\delta_k) \rVert < \lVert F(x_k) \rVert \) or the iteration cap is hit) instead of always taking the full \( \alpha=1 \) step -- trades some convergence speed for robustness when the plain Newton step would overshoot.
math_notes.algebra_newton_system_fd: Same Newton iteration as `algebra_newton_system`, but the Jacobian is approximated via forward finite differences instead of requiring the caller to hand-derive one: \( J_{ij} \approx \dfrac{F_i(x + h e_j) - F_i(x)}{h} \) for a small step \( h \) and the \( j \)-th standard basis vector \( e_j \) -- costs an extra \( O(n) \) evaluations of \( F \) per Newton step to build the full Jacobian this way.
